scenes.headline: How an RL loss survives a sampler that drifts
scenes.sub: Off-policy drift, the ratio p over q, and Tinker's StableReinforce
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cleat! Your sampler and your learner never quite agree. Here's why that breaks reinforcement learning.

scenes.text: StableReinforce trains only on samples the server recorded, and pulls the learner back toward the sampler that drew them.
scenes.mark: pulls the learner back toward the sampler
scenes.say: The idea: train only on samples the server recorded, and pull the learner back toward the sampler that drew them.

steps.say: The learner keeps training while the sampler runs weights a few steps old, with its own numerics.
The server records every sequence it samples, and gives each one an id.
Every scored token must point back to a recorded sequence.
Then the loss updates the learner. Its main term is not published.

scenes.title: Every loss is the same gradient
scenes.text: grad = sum c_t * A_t * grad log p

parts.say: Each sampled token gets its advantage.

parts.note: push this token up or down
parts.say: Times the push on that token's log probability.

parts.note: the one number each loss changes
parts.say: And one coefficient. That is the only thing the losses disagree about.

scenes.title: Two ways to set the coefficient

left.title: Follow the ratio
items: Step grows with p over q
One token can get 55 times its advantage
left.say: Importance sampling follows the ratio, and so does PPO when the advantage is negative. One token can get an enormous step.

right.title: Bound the coefficient
items: REINFORCE, CISPO, truncated or masked ratios
right.say: Bounded coefficients cap that step. A little bias, and the run stays alive.

scenes.title: The part that is published
scenes.text: L_KL = beta * sum (log q - log p)

parts.note: sampler versus learner, per sampled token
parts.say: The docs publish one term: the gap between sampler and learner, on each sampled token.
Scaled by a small beta, it keeps the learner near the sampler.

steps.say: In a published study with low precision sampling, the baselines climb, then collapse.
And the mismatch between sampler and trainer grows before they fall.

scenes.title: Toy run, sampler 32 steps stale
scenes.note: Final reward, tiny CPU simulation, 3 seeds
scenes.say: In my small simulation, with the sampler thirty-two steps stale, the ratio-following losses collapse. The bounded ones don't.

scenes.text: A step that grows with the ratio is what breaks. Bound the coefficient, and watch the sampler to learner gap.
scenes.say: A step that grows with the ratio is what breaks. Bound the coefficient, and watch the sampler to learner gap.

recap: Drift gives every token a ratio
StableReinforce publishes its KL, not its core
scenes.say: Drift gives every token a ratio. Unbounded coefficients blow up. And Stable Reinforce publishes its K L term, but not its core.
